![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/54ff64195ccfadddfe2b3ca0bb9e193147fedae20d8dae6a53a5ecddc3c26f5d.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-16y$ for $x\le 0$ and $z\ge 0,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$  represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $8$ centered at $(0,-8,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-16y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-16y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-16\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/868214a1c2b30da5b16b7f0c307b369bdc9f2d2201ee0ad5a3f5da2a8bdc6f49.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\sqrt{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{-16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
